turns.text: The bad ear throbs once, a weather-warning arriving a full breath ahead of the storm itself — an old notch in the fur that never closed right, aching worse whenever the pressure drops. Paw already moving before the ache finishes: toward paper. Somewhere close, wet paper, ink-bitter, glue-sweet, stapled fresh to a post since the last rain. Can't not go to it. Never could.

the fog here doesn't lift so much as thicken and thin, laminate-dust hanging in it fine as flour, every lamppost wearing a jacket of notices three and four layers deep, some peeling, some fresh enough to still smell of the machine that printed them. a kiosk screen on the corner scrolls text too small and too fast for anything but a very patient eye, looping the same six paragraphs since before the fog remembers starting. somewhere close, a fixed speaker hums awake between announcements, warming its throat.

Tongue finds the newest layer first, always the newest layer, peeling a corner up with teeth before the taste even registers — glue going bitter-sweet-bitter as it softens, paper going soft and gray at the edges the way good paper never stays good for long. Ears swivel toward the speaker's throat-clearing hum. Old habit, older than tonight: whatever that voice says next, it'll be worth chewing over.

the speaker finds its rhythm and holds it — addendum nineteen, effective immediately, superseding addendum eighteen, which is hereby void, except where it isn't, see addendum seventeen — a flat voice with no rise or fall in it, wearing the same groove it wore last week and the week before. underneath it, bleeding in from two blocks over, something louder and shinier fights for the same air: a livestream feed stapled to a taller pole, tagged HAPPYWARE in scrolling corporate pink, a grin held too wide for too long, glitching every few seconds into teeth that don't quite line up with the jaw.

Two signals fighting for the same stretch of air, and neither one wins clean — the flat droning clauses cut through the grinning static and back again, addendum and glitch-tooth trading the same three feet of fog. Claws rake one long scratch down the newest notice anyway, over the old bitter-chemical mark some stranger left there last week, over the one before that. This post belongs to whoever keeps coming back to it. Tonight, that's still this cat.

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

the scratch is still fresh when the fog answers with a different pressure entirely — rotor-thrum arriving low and even, a compliance drone working the block on a route that always runs this hour, scanning notice boards for anything unlicensed, unstapled, unpaid-for. its searchlight throws the kiosk's scroll into hard white relief, catches the HAPPYWARE feed's too-wide grin and slides past it without slowing, because a grin that big is always, technically, licensed.

Flat against the post's cold base before the light finishes arriving, weight held low, breath held lower. The drone's scan doesn't care about a cat, has never cared about a cat, but caring isn't the same as safe, and the old ear knows the difference in its own private ache. Wait it out. Count the addendum's droning clauses instead of counting heartbeats — nineteen, eighteen, void, void, still here.

the drone finishes its pass and banks off toward the next block without ever dipping its light low enough to find fur against concrete, rotor-thrum fading back into the general hum fog always carries. what it leaves behind, dislodged by its own downwash, is a single loose sheet — torn free from somewhere higher up the post, tumbling once, catching against a drainpipe grate before the wind can take it further.

That loose sheet is worth more than the ones still stapled down — anything the wind wants that badly is worth wanting back. Low run to the drainpipe, one paw pinning a corner before the next gust can argue, teeth closing on the edge and hauling the whole sheet flat against the wet concrete. Ink smell floods stronger here, fresher, less chewed-over than anything upstream.

flat under a paw, the sheet turns out to be three layers fused wet-to-wet — the newest addendum on top, and under it, half-dissolved, an older notice gone soft enough to read only by taste: a bounty tier, numbers instead of a face, expired weeks ago and never taken down, the kind of paper the fog swallows instead of burying. none of it says anything that hasn't already been said somewhere else in this district, in some other voice, on some other loop.

Nothing under the top layer but more of the same, dissolving expired numbers that never meant food or warmth to begin with, and the disappointment lands exactly where hunger already was — quiet, familiar, undramatic. Lets the sheet go. It doesn't fly this time, just sits there soaking, already becoming next week's bottom layer for some other night's chewing.

/\___/\
    ( o   o )   >> scanning...
     )  Y  (    >> ears: antenna mod v2
    (   |   )
     \_____/

past the drainpipe the fog thins enough to show the HAPPYWARE feed full-size for the first time all night, mounted three stories up on a pole nobody's licensed to climb — the grin glitches wide, then wider, unicode fracturing along the jaw into something with too many teeth for the shape it's wearing, before snapping back to seventeen hours of unbroken cheer. a caption crawls underneath, half in real letters, half in the broken kind: TODAY'S MESSAGE — YOU ARE NOT TRAPPED — the words repeating past the point of meaning anything at all.

Ears flatten hard at the glitching jaw, not from danger exactly, more the way a bad smell makes the whole face want to close — something about a mouth that wide holding still that long. Eyes drop off it fast, tail low, aimed back into the fog where the addendum's flat drone still loops its bloodless nineteen-eighteen-void, which is at least honest about being nothing worth feeling anything over.

the fog closes back in behind, swallowing the grin's pink glow into general gray, and the district settles into its usual layered hum — droning clauses, dripping laminate, one kiosk screen scrolling paragraphs nobody alive has finished reading. underfoot the pavement runs drier here, a strip of awning holding most of the mist off a doorway nobody uses anymore.

Doorway's dry strip is enough. Circles twice against the old wood, working the bad ear's ache down to background static the way lying still always eventually manages, tongue running once more over the ink-bitter aftertaste still clinging behind the teeth. Tomorrow the post outside will grow a new layer over tonight's scratch mark. That's fine. There'll be a tomorrow to scratch it again.

above the doorway the fog keeps its slow churn, addendum bleeding into glitch-grin bleeding into rain that hasn't decided to properly start, the whole district looping its paperwork through another indifferent hour. nothing here gets resolved, only reissued, and the district files tonight's scratch mark exactly where it files everything else: pending, unread, superseded by tomorrow.
